rationale: Executive Order 7628 (June 8, 1937, Arkansas) temporarily withdrew one 79.50-acre tract (T. 4 S., R. 28 W., sec. 31, lots 1 and 5 of NW1/4) from settlement, location, sale or entry for classification, 'until revoked by the President or by act of Congress'. Executive Order 7719, signed October 8, 1937 (2 FR 2465), includes the same tract in the Ouachita National Forest and states that its reservation 'supersedes the temporary withdrawal of the above-described land made by Executive Order No. 7628 of June 8, 1937'. That supersedes the whole continuing command (the withdrawal; section 1's revocation of Executive Order 6964 as to the tract was performed on signing), so the order had no operative force on 2026-10-14. History observations: the OFR note 'Amends: EO 6964' describes this order's effect on an earlier order, and the 1989 printed codification lists the order under public lands as excluded, not ended; neither shows continuing effect. No earlier end, partial-scope limit or saving wording was found: Executive Order 7719 preserves nothing of Executive Order 7628, and the land stays reserved under 7719 as an independent reservation. The USC and eCFR machine searches (through 2026-10-14) have no hit for this number.
